newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha jumps in bullish sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha jumps in bullish sentiment.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices jumped higher on Monday fuelled by gains in crude prices on Friday and bullish sentiment based on expectations of strong Asian demand, traders said.
Open-spec naphtha for first-half May was assessed at about $235.50/237.50, up from Friday levels of $231.00/232.00, and second-half May at $232.00/234.00, up from $228.00/229.00.

In afternoon trade, first-half June switched hands at $229.00, up $2.00 from early morning levels of $227.00, traders said. On Friday, first-half June traded at $226.25 and second-half May at $229.50, they said.
"Sentiment is bullish," a trader said. "Asian market prices were not seriously dented by the recent imports from Europe, showing demand here is strong," he said.

Inter-month spreads were a touch wider with the one-month spread from first-half May at around $6.50, up from Friday's $6.00. Second-half May/second-half June was assessed at $4.75/5.50, compared to $4.50/5.00.
The backwardation was seen widening slightly, traders said.
Japanese end-users are keeping to the sidelines, but could emerge as buyers of May cargoes by the end of this week, they said. -- Tokyo Energy Desk +81-3-5473-3708
